name: SelFee: Iterative Self-Revising LLM Empowered by Self-Feedback Generation
authors: Seonghyeon Ye*, Yongrae Jo*, Doyoung Kim*, Sungdong Kim, Hyeonbin Hwang, Minjoon Seo (KAIST AI; LK Lab / KAIST)
venue: Blog post + code/model release (KAIST), May 31, 2023; not a formal peer-reviewed venue (no arXiv paper)
code_url: https://github.com/kaistAI/SelFee (model diff weights: kaist-ai/selfee-7b-delta, kaist-ai/selfee-13b-delta; training data: https://huggingface.co/datasets/kaist-ai/selfee-train)
reflection_type: verbal-self-critique (model generates its own natural-language feedback and self-revises; the self-critique-and-revise capability is distilled into the model via supervised fine-tuning, i.e. a learned self-feedback generator rather than a separate learned critic model)
feedback_source: self-generated (the fine-tuned model produces its own feedback sequences with no external tools/retrieval/oracle at inference time). NOTE: the SFT training data was distilled from ChatGPT, and for the Math/Code/Flan portions ChatGPT generated feedback while conditioned on the available ground-truth answers; at inference time SelFee uses no ground truth.
iteration_structure: iterative-refine (autoregressive answer -> feedback -> revised answer -> feedback ... chain), but the entire iterative loop is emitted within a single forward pass / single inference; model autonomously decides when to stop ('Revision is not needed.') or can be forced to a minimum number of revisions
reflection_object: output content (the model's own answer to an instruction) via an interleaved natural-language reasoning/feedback chain; the revision target is the response text, not a reasoning chain over an environment, action trajectory, or external memory
learning_locus: gradient_weight_update (the self-feedback + self-revision behavior is baked into the LLaMA weights via supervised fine-tuning on 178K ChatGPT-distilled feedback+revision instances; at inference there is no weight update, the iterative refinement is purely generated)
requires_training: SFT (supervised fine-tuning of LLaMA 7B/13B on 178K instruction->answer+feedback-chain+revision sequences; 3 epochs, lr 2e-5, global batch 128, max length 2048, via FastChat). No RL or preference optimization.
reward_or_critic_model: self-as-judge baked into the model: the same model generates its own feedback used to drive revisions. Training supervision is knowledge distilled from ChatGPT (teacher LLM) as feedback/revision generator; no separately trained reward model and no verifiable reward at inference.
distillation_target: model-weights (ChatGPT-generated self-feedback-and-revision trajectories are distilled into the LLaMA model parameters so the student can self-feedback and self-revise without the teacher, tools, retrieval, or in-context demonstrations)
emergent_vs_engineered: engineered: the reflective self-feedback/self-revision behavior is induced by supervised fine-tuning on explicitly constructed feedback+revision chains (teacher distillation), not RL-emergent. The data-generation scaffold (ChatGPT generates answer, then feedback, then conditional revision) is prompt/scaffold-engineered; the resulting behavior is then internalized in weights.
memory_type: short-term/scratchpad (the feedback+revision chain functions as an in-context scratchpad within a single inference); no persistent episodic memory, skill library, or external store
memory_persistence: within-episode (the feedback/revision chain exists only within the single inference for one instruction; nothing persists across queries). The 'learning' that persists across tasks lives in the fine-tuned weights, not in a memory module.
memory_curation_mechanism: n/a (no explicit memory store to curate; the model autonomously truncates the revision chain when feedback signals 'Revision is not needed.' or a max-iteration cap is hit, but this is generation termination, not memory curation)
error_localization_granularity: response-level (feedback critiques and revises the whole answer/response holistically and assigns a quality score; not step-level, token-level, or block-level localization)
intra_task_vs_inter_task: intra-task at inference (refines a single answer within one task via the feedback/revision chain). Cross-task generalization comes from the SFT weights rather than from transferred experience artifacts.
failure_recovery_vs_avoidance: post-hoc-revision (the model produces an initial answer then critiques and revises it within the same inference); it is in-flight self-revision of output content rather than retry-with-reset across episodes
task_domains: general instruction-following / open-ended generation (creative writing, long-form text), with training data also spanning math, code, QA/reasoning (Flan); evaluated primarily as a general chat assistant
benchmarks: Vicuna evaluation setting (80 diverse queries, GPT-4-as-judge with bidirectional/position-debiased scoring, relative to ChatGPT). Training data sourced from Stanford Alpaca, AQUA/GSM8K/MATH, Conala/DeepMind Code Contest/DrRepair/MBPP, FLAN collection, ShareGPT.
headline_result: On the Vicuna 80-query GPT-4 evaluation (relative score vs ChatGPT=100), SelFee 7B/13B outperform LLaMA, Alpaca, Vicuna, and Guanaco and are roughly comparable to ChatGPT. SelFee-13B with >=3 enforced revisions scores 101.4 vs ChatGPT; SelFee-13B with no enforced revisions scores 98.2. Notably a 7B model with >=3 revisions (101.4) beats a 13B model with no enforced revisions (98.2).
baselines: LLaMA, Stanford Alpaca, Vicuna, Guanaco (open-source LLaMA-based instruction models), and ChatGPT (closed teacher model, used as the 100-point reference); also internal ablation across SelFee variants with different minimum required revisions
gains_vs_baseline: Versus the strongest open-source baseline (Vicuna), SelFee is reported to win on the Vicuna setting and reach near-ChatGPT relative scores. Key reported delta is internal: enforcing a minimum of 3 revisions on SelFee-13B raises the relative score to 101.4 vs 98.2 with no enforced revisions (~+3.2 points), and the 7B@3-revisions matches/beats 13B@0-revisions (101.4 vs 98.2), supporting the inference-compute-scaling claim. Exact per-baseline numeric deltas beyond these are presented as win-rate bar charts rather than tabulated numbers.
compute_cost_profile: Training: SFT of LLaMA 7B/13B on 178K instances, 3 epochs (one-time cost). Inference: a single forward pass but generates a longer sequence (answer + feedback + multiple revisions), so token/compute cost scales roughly with the number of revisions; enforcing >=3 revisions increases generated tokens vs a single-shot answer. The paper frames this as scaling inference computation (longer generation) being more effective than scaling model size.
known_limitations: Authors state SelFee (7B/13B) underperforms ChatGPT and lacks knowledge in math, reasoning, factuality, and coding (a common limitation of LLaMA-finetuned models attributed to weak base models, echoing 'The False Promise of Imitating Proprietary LLMs'). Evaluation itself is acknowledged as limited: only 80 queries, GPT-4-judge positional bias, inconsistency and unreliability; authors explicitly say to take claims 'with a grain of salt.' Forcing revisions when unnecessary can degrade quality.
oracle_or_external_feedback_dependency: intrinsic-only at inference (no external tool/verifier/oracle used when running SelFee). However, the distilled training signal is not purely intrinsic: ChatGPT served as teacher, and for Math/Code/Flan subsets feedback was generated by ChatGPT conditioned on ground-truth answers, so oracle/teacher information leaks into the training data even though inference is intrinsic.
self_correction_efficacy: net-positive in the reported setting: enforcing more revisions (up to 3) improves the Vicuna-setting relative score (98.2 -> 101.4 for 13B), and revision-enabled models beat non-revising larger models. Task-dependent though: gains concentrate in open-ended/creative generation; forcing unnecessary revisions can reduce quality, and the model does not overcome base-model weaknesses on math/reasoning/factuality/coding.
calibration_effect: not-measured (no calibration / confidence-accuracy analysis reported; the model emits a self-assessed quality score in feedback but no calibration study is provided)
failure_attribution_capability: n/a (SelFee is a self-correction generation method, not a failure-attribution / error-localization study; its feedback assigns a holistic quality score and a revise/no-revise decision rather than attributing failures to specific steps or agents)
failure_mode_addressed: Targets low-quality / under-refined single-shot responses by forcing iterative self-revision; mitigates 'superficial single-pass answers' for open-ended generation. Does not address (and is limited by) base-model knowledge gaps in math, reasoning, factuality, and coding; risk of over-revision (degrading correct answers when revision is forced unnecessarily), loosely related to MAST-style 'superficial self-reflection' / over-correction failure modes.
dataset_or_benchmark_released: Yes: the 178K-instance SelFee training dataset of instruction->answer+feedback+revision chains is released (https://huggingface.co/datasets/kaist-ai/selfee-train); also released model diff weights (selfee-7b-delta, selfee-13b-delta), full data-augmentation/training/inference/evaluation code, and inference outputs + GPT-4 review scores. No new evaluation benchmark introduced (reuses the Vicuna 80-query setting).
builds_on: Reflexion (Shinn et al., 2023); Self-Refine (Madaan et al., 2023); Self-Correction (Welleck et al., 2022, 'Generating Sequences by Learning to Self-Correct'); RL4F (Akyurek et al., 2023); PEER (Schick et al., 2022); Self-Critiquing / Self-Critique (Saunders et al., 2022). Engineering base: Stanford Alpaca, Vicuna/FastChat, LLaMA; data from Alpaca, AQUA, GSM8K, MATH, Conala, DeepMind Code Contest, DrRepair, MBPP, FLAN collection, ShareGPT; teacher distillation from ChatGPT.
extended_by_or_inspired: Cited/positioned as a training-based self-correction baseline in survey/analysis works, e.g. Kamoi et al. (TACL 2024) 'When Can LLMs Actually Correct Their Own Mistakes? A Critical Survey of Self-Correction' (notes SelFee trains a model to emulate self-correction); the ICSF self-feedback survey (Liang et al., arXiv:2407.14507); 'A Survey on LLM-as-a-Judge'; and related KAIST follow-ups such as Volcano (Lee et al., NAACL 2024, self-feedback-guided multimodal revision).
citation_count: ~80 (Google Scholar, per author Yongrae Jo's profile entry 'Selfee: Iterative self-revising llm... Blog post, 2023', as of June 2026). Not indexed with a count on Semantic Scholar because it is a blog post rather than an arXiv/peer-reviewed paper.
reasoning_model_native: no (predates and does not target o1/R1-style reasoning models with built-in reflection; SelFee instead manufactures reflective behavior in a 2023-era LLaMA via SFT). The single-pass interleaved feedback/revision chain is conceptually a precursor to such models' inline self-correction.
on_policy_distillation_link: Off-policy distillation: the student is trained on ChatGPT-generated (teacher-policy) feedback/revision trajectories, i.e. offline SFT on teacher outputs rather than on-policy distillation on the student's own rollouts. Relevant to OPD discussions as a contrasting off-policy 'imitate the teacher's self-correction' approach (and a target of the 'False Promise of Imitating Proprietary LLMs' critique).
sample_efficiency: Training: 178K SFT instances, 3 epochs (LLaMA 7B/13B). Inference: best reported quality reached at a minimum of ~3 self-revisions per query; beyond 3 enforced revisions does not further help, and forcing revisions when unneeded can hurt.
